rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the slave and master do not settle the contract matter, the society's responsible authorities resolve the dispute.
rows.anchor: if some dispute arises, then those responsible for the society will settle it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the dispute remains unresolved, a court of law gives the final decision.
rows.anchor: If the need still remains, then the matter will be decided by a court of law.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The owner must assess whether a slave has the ability and willingness to meet the emancipation contract.
rows.anchor: slave owner should see if his slave has the ability and the will to fulfil the commitment

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The capacity condition guards against a slave using a contract request to solicit money without being able to work, then relying on begging.
rows.anchor: has no ability to work, and he uses this plight to ask for monetary help from people and even make it a pretext to take to beggary as a profession

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because contracted slaves were to receive public help, an incapable person might seek the contract and become a social burden; inability to pay could also cause disputes.
rows.anchor: capacity or ability to work and make an effort themselves, ultimately becoming a burden on the society

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The capacity condition cannot obstruct a capable slave's freedom because society and, if needed, the court decide disputes.
rows.anchor: the final verdict, in case of dispute, rested with the society and the court of law

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A capable slave who says the master is using the condition to block freedom can appeal to community elders or a court.
rows.anchor: he could also take his case to the elders of the society and even to a court of law if needed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to give slaves from God's provision urges society, especially the affluent, to fund the freedom of those seeking it generously.
rows.anchor: urge the society to spend generously and courageously from the wealth God has blessed them with on all slaves who want obtain freedom

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appeal to God's gift stirs gratitude, and spending for slave emancipation is spending in God's cause.
rows.anchor: they should not hesitate to spend from what God has given them for His own the cause

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earliest authorities unanimously held that slaves seeking freedom may receive zakāh and public-treasury funds.
rows.anchor: our earliest authorities are unanimous that such slaves can be helped through zakāh money and through the public treasury

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's allocation for freeing slaves establishes a dedicated public-treasury category.
rows.anchor: a special head has been fixed in the public treasury for the liberation of slaves

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The right to mukātabat applies to slave-women as well as slave-men, as the general wording and Prophetic and Companion practice show.
rows.anchor: Just as Islam has given this right of mukātabat to slave-men, it has also given it to slave-women

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Narratives cite the cases of Barīrah and Juwayriyah as examples involving this right for women.
rows.anchor: The incidents of Barīrah (rta) and Juwayriyah are mentioned in narratives as examples

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The law made emancipation broadly possible for capable male and female slaves; those content with their situation or unable to work remained.
rows.anchor: only those slaves remained who were

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A blanket liberation of people unable to support themselves would remove their masters' support and leave them a burden on society.
rows.anchor: they would have been deprived of the support of their masters and would not have been able to support themselves too

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word fatayāt here means slave-women and was chosen to raise their social status and respect.
rows.anchor: The word ﻓَﺘَﻴٰﺖ here is used for “slave-women” and the purpose of using this word for them is to increase their status and respect in the society

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatā is the feminine of fatā: the latter means a young boy and the former a young girl.
rows.anchor: Just as the latter means a young boy, the former means a young girl

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The respectful change in terminology sought to build slaves' self-esteem and lead people to regard them as their brethren.
rows.anchor: The purpose of changing this word was to engender self-esteem in them and to direct the attention of people to change their conceptions about them and regard them from their own brethren

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about slave-women wanting chastity describes a situation; it is not a condition on the ruling.
rows.anchor: are not a condition; they depict a situation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Criminalizing fornication, encouraging slave marriage, and opening emancipation naturally encouraged women forced into prostitution to wish for a chaste life.
rows.anchor: Those among them who were forced to adopt prostitution by their masters must have wished to lead a chaste life

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrite ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy, who instigated the ifk incident, is said in historical references to have run such a brothel.
rows.anchor: The famous hypocrite ‘Abdull āh ibn Ubayy, who had instigated the incident of ifk, also ran a similar den

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masters who profited from prostitution used every means to prevent slave-women from choosing chastity, and the verse addresses them.
rows.anchor: Thus they used all ill-means to stop them from leading chaste lives

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forgives women forced into prostitution but not the masters who force them, and they should consider their fate.
rows.anchor: God will forgive these women if they are forced to prostitution but he will not forgive their masters who are playing this heinous role

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author refers to later cases in which people running prostitution dens were stoned at the Prophet's direction.
rows.anchor: certain people who ran prostitution-dens were stoned to death at the Prophet’s directive in later phases

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 34 renews the sūrah's recurring warning, whose examples occur earlier and at 24:46; the author discussed the wisdom of this repetition while explaining its first verse.
rows.anchor: I have already indicated the wisdom for this repetition

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's reference to the parable of earlier peoples points ahead to the parable in verse 35.
rows.anchor: allude to the parable which is mentioned in verse 35 ahead

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those without fear of God are unaffected by explanations, counsel, or advice and will meet their own fate.
rows.anchor: people who have no fear of God, no explanation or counsel or advice has any effect on them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After explaining slavery guidance verse by verse, the author gathers the relevant teachings here to clear up misconceptions.
rows.anchor: I would like to comprehensively state the teachings regarding slavery that have been referred to earlier at various instances

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Slavery was not an institution of Islam; it was temporarily tolerated because of the international and national conditions of the time.
rows.anchor: Slavery was never a part of Islam. It was tolerated temporarily keeping in view the international and national circumstances of those times

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sudden abolition could empower enemies and create serious social and economic problems.
rows.anchor: given an opportunity to the enemies and at same time created many social and economic problems within the society

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the contemporary setting, victors conventionally enslaved prisoners of war, slave markets were extensive, and most households had slaves.
rows.anchor: the conventional way to resolve the issue of prisoners of war was that they were made slaves by the victors

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many slaves could not support themselves; their masters bore that legal burden, while release could leave them dependent on begging.
rows.anchor: their masters would bear their burden by law. Once set free, the only option left for them would be to take to beggary

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The risks of withdrawing support from slave-women were especially grave, including moral evils, and the treasury could not support all of them.
rows.anchor: Withdrawal of support from them could have created many moral evils. The public treasury obviously was not in a position to financially support all of them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam therefore used gradual emancipation of able slaves so they could become useful members of society without creating the anticipated harms.
rows.anchor: a gradual strategy of emancipating able slaves to make them a useful part of the society

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet urged kind treatment, while sharīʿah made masters' duties toward slaves part of their legal rights, curbing masters' former tyrannical authority.
rows.anchor: regarded their rights which their masters owed to them as part of the sharī‘ ah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Freeing slaves was prescribed as expiation for certain crimes and sins and was also considered charity.
rows.anchor: For the expiation of some crimes and sins, liberation of slaves was prescribed. This liberation was also regarded as an act of charity

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All capable male and female slaves were directed to be married.
rows.anchor: It was directed that all capable slave-men and slave-women should be wedded

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A dedicated zakāh and public-treasury allocation for freeing slaves was established to accelerate emancipation.
rows.anchor: An independent head was fixed in public treasury and zakāh for the liberation of slaves

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After fornication was criminalized, masters' prostitution dens were eliminated and secret continuation brought exemplary punishment.
rows.anchor: prostitution-dens – set up masters to force slave-women to this sin – were done away with

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some people, men and women, guilty of running prostitution dens were stoned to death at the Prophet's behest.
rows.anchor: some men and women guilty of this crime were stoned to death at the behest of the Prophet (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People were told to replace the humiliating labels for enslaved men and women with respectful terms to change old conceptions.
rows.anchor: people were asked to use the word  and ﻓَﺘَﺎةٌ for them so that age-old conceptions about them should change

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For prisoners of war, some prominent leaders were executed while others were released with or without ransom.
rows.anchor: though certain prominent leaders were executed but others were released with or without ransom

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving mukātabat legal status made it easy for every able male or female slave to gain freedom.
rows.anchor: mukātabat was given a legal status. After this, it became very easy for all able slave-man and slave-woman to become free

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community and treasury were to support contracts; this law practically ended slavery, leaving only slaves unable to work and be useful.
rows.anchor: people were urged to help and support them regarding their freedom from their masters, and for this a head was fixed in the public treasury. This law practically abolished slavery

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining unable-to-work slaves were better off supported than freed into dependency and forced begging, which would also burden society.
rows.anchor: This option was not only best for them but also for the society otherwise they would have become a burden and would have been forced to adopt beggary as a profession

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Detailed Qur'an and ḥadīth arguments support these measures; the author omits them to avoid prolonging this discussion, noting most had already been explained.
rows.anchor: I can present them but this may prolong the discussion

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable passage in verses 35–40 casts light over the sūrah's parts and depicts faith and disbelief through inner and outer light and darkness.
rows.anchor: They cast their shadow on all its constituents. The parable of belief and disbelief is mentioned in them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage shows faith's radiance in a person's inner and outer self through deeds in individual and collective life.
rows.anchor: The radiance of faith in the inner and outer self of a person becomes evident through it. Described are the deeds which manifest themselves in the individual and collective lives of people

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It also portrays disbelief as darkness engulfing a person's inner and outer self.
rows.anchor: the darkness that engulfs the inner and outer self of a person because of disbelief is portrayed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's people denied only Noah, yet the plural messengers is used because all messengers conveyed the same message; rejecting Noah thus rejects every messenger, and rejecters share a mentality and fate. Abraham's story warns Muhammad's opponents.
rows.anchor: The people of Noah (sws) had only denied one messenger: Noah (sws). However, the plural “messengers” is used

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Acceptance and rejection reflect a people's mentality; rejecting Noah's message amounts to rejecting every messenger, whose rejecters share a mentality and fate. Abraham's story warns those rejecting Muhammad.
rows.anchor: the real basis of acceptance or rejection is the mentality of people

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's question asking whether they fear God carries a warning.
rows.anchor: The expression “Do you people not have fear?” carries an element of warning in it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Noah a trusted messenger shows he is neither a fabricator nor false claimant, but honestly conveys what God commands.
rows.anchor: as God’s messenger, with full honesty he is presenting them what God is asking him to

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To escape God's punishment, the people must abandon rebellion, fear God's grasp, obey Noah, and stop following rebellious leaders who lead them to destruction.
rows.anchor: The way to do this is to obey Noah (sws) and stop following these rebellious people who were leading them to destruction
